result:
None of the three solutions reaches the answer I get, which is 1/3.

**Upper bound.** Two holes cannot share a boundary point, so no two holes can touch even at a corner. An optimal configuration uses 1×1 holes, and their cells must form a king-independent set. Such a set has density at most 1/4, because each 2×2 block contains at most one hole cell. The polyomino has at least 3 cells for every hole, so h/n ≤ (1/4)/(3/4) = 1/3. This rules out Solution 1 (1/2) and Solution 2 (3/8).

**Construction.** Place holes at all cells (2i, 2j) with 0 ≤ i, j < m. Let P be every other cell of the bounding box, plus a surrounding ring. Then P is connected, the hole boundaries are pairwise disjoint and disjoint from the outer boundary, and n ≈ 3m² against h = m² holes. So h/n → 1/3.

**Why Solution 3 fails.** Its Lemma 1 is wrong. A cell may touch two holes on opposite sides, since the two edges involved share no vertex. Holes at (0,0) and (2,0) can share the neighbour (1,0). The bound n ≥ 4h therefore does not hold, and the true limit exceeds its 1/4.

Since the true value is 1/3, all three final answers are wrong. Solution 3 is the nearest, because its claimed value is a valid lower bound for the limit and its construction is a legitimate one. I choose it only as the least-wrong option.

CHOICE: 3
